newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers from lows, could extend decline.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers from lows, could extend decline.

text.p: The ringgit recovered slightly from its morning lows and was expected to undergo further correction early next week, dealers said on Friday.
They said the sharp rise of the dollar against ringgit in the last three days needed correction as many speculators were left short of the Malaysian currency.
"It all depends on how dollar/ringgit closes today. If it closes below 2.5270, then maybe it will go down further," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank in Kuala Lumpur.
He said a lot of stop-losses were building up around 2.5220 a dollar level, which if broken would trigger more falls.
"If the stop-losses are big, then the big guys will push it down further," another dealer said.
But, dealers said dollar/ringgit continued to be well bidded and the Singapore dollar was on an uptrend against the ringgit.

In the morning, the ringgit fell to 2.53 a dollar before recovering to 2.5255/65 at 0800 GMT against 2.5265/75 at close of trading on Thursday. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5576/81 a ringgit against 0.0.5574/80
The ringgit hit a six-month low against the U.S. dollar early on Thursday.
